Matbucha — The Cooked Pepper-Tomato of the Salad Course

Moroccan · Easy · Makes about 600 g (one jar)

Jump to Recipe Method Troubleshooting Storage
The matbucha is the salad course's own cooked jar — the peppers and tomatoes simmered down to the dark, glossy, concentrated spread that the North African table runs beside the bread's ceremony: not the dip of the raw salsa's register but the long-cooked concentrate, the Moroccan-Maghrebi kitchen's answer to what the market's summer glut becomes at the jar's patience.

Quantities live in the recipe card.

Ingredients

- **The matbucha's law: the reduction is the recipe.** The raw-vegetable salsa's freshness is not this jar's register — the matbucha runs the summer's peppers and tomatoes cooked down past the water's release, past the sauce's stage, to the dark spread's concentration where the spoon's trail holds on the bread's face. The hour's simmer is the honest minimum; the pot that runs wet is the salsa wearing the matbucha's name. - **The bridge:** the #105 mechouia (the fire-roasted pepper salad, the pantry's later seat) runs the raw-roasted register's sister craft; this jar runs the cooked concentrate — and the #61 shakshuka's base and the matbucha run the same pepper-tomato spine at the two registers: the shakshuka's quick pan and the matbucha's long jar.

Matbucha — The Cooked Pepper-Tomato of the Salad Course

Prep: 15 min · Cook: 1 h · Total: 1 h 15 min · Makes about 600 g (one jar)

Ingredients

Ingredients

  • 4 red bell peppers (about 800 g), roasted and peeled, or the charred register's honesty: see the method
  • 1.2 kg ripe tomatoes (about 6–8 medium), grated
  • 1 head of garlic (about 10 cloves, 40 g), sliced
  • 1–2 hot green chiles (about 20 g), the heat's own dial
  • 4 tbsp olive oil (about 50 g)
  • 1 tsp sweet paprika (about 3 g)
  • 1 tsp ground cumin (about 3 g)
  • 1½ tsp salt (about 9 g)
  • 1 tsp sugar (about 4 g), the tomatoes' acid's mercy

Instructions

  1. **The peppers' char (20 minutes, the flame's or the oven's law).** The peppers charred whole over the open flame, the grill, or the oven's broiler at its highest (the 250 °C register) — the skins' full blackening, the flesh's steam-softening — then the bowl's cover and the 15-minute sweat, the skins' rub-off under the water's film, and the flesh's torn strips with every seed's honesty removed. Checkpoint — the char's proof: the pepper's flesh runs the soft sweetness of the fully-roasted (the char's smoke at the skin's face, the flesh within the deep red's tenderness) — the under-charred pepper runs the raw's edge, and the matbucha's whole register begins at this roast's honesty.
  2. **The base's build (10 minutes).** The oil in the wide pan over the medium; the garlic and chiles softened 3 minutes at the oil's warmth (never browned — the garlic's scorch runs the whole pot's bitterness), the paprika and cumin bloomed in the oil's edge for the 30-second wake. Checkpoint — the bloom's law, the #91's own carried: the spices' fragrance released in the oil's warmth before the tomatoes' flood — the raw-powder's addition straight to the wet pot runs the dusty's flatness, and the 30-second bloom runs the whole jar's perfume.
  3. **The long reduction (45–50 minutes).** The grated tomatoes and the torn peppers in with the salt and the sugar; the pan brought to the gentle, steady simmer — uncovered, the wide pan's surface running the evaporation's whole work — and the pot stirred at the 10-minute intervals' patience, the splatter's guard at the latter stages, until the dark concentration arrives. Checkpoint — the reduction's proof at the 45-minute mark: the spoon's trail drawn across the pan's base holds its clean line for the seconds' count — the water's departure whole, the color run to the deep brick-red's darkness, the oil's red-gold breaking through at the trail's edges. The matbucha's spread-register runs at this line: thick enough to hold the bread's smear without the drip.
  4. **The jar and the rest.** The matbucha packed to the clean jar, the oil's thin seal at the surface, and the jar cooled before the seal's close. Checkpoint — eating test: the bread's swipe — the deep, sweet-smoky concentration (the char's smoke and the long simmer's caramel running together), the garlic's rounded warmth, the cumin's earth beneath, the chile's slow heat at the finish — the acid's brightness rounded by the sugar's mercy and the hour's reduction, never the raw tomato's sharpness. It should taste like the summer's whole argument, settled and jarred — the market's glut run to the dark spoon's economy.

Troubleshooting

SymptomCauseFix
Jar wet, sauce-run at the breadThe reduction's shortfallThe spoon-trail's line — the hour's honest minimum
Jar bitterThe garlic's brown or the peppers' under-charThe oil's warmth only; the full char's law
Flavor flat, dustyThe spices unbloomedThe 30-second oil-bloom before the wet

Storage, Make-Ahead & Variations

- The sealed jar keeps 2 weeks refrigerated (the oil seal's covenant carried), improving through the first week's marriage — the make-ahead's own gift, the Friday jar and the week's table. The variations: the hotter chile's dial, the smoked paprika's autumn register, the #92 preserved lemon's threads at the finish for the city's school.
